I need to hear from open-source, privacy, commercial-contracts, and export counsel before I can give final legal approval for the release package. Can each of you walk me through where things stand on your respective reviews?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical licensing issue. I reviewed the dependency manifest and found that the toolkit links to a core library distributed only under AGPL-3.0. This means the release must use AGPL-3.0-only as its license, and we must provide the corresponding source for the linked toolkit code. I've had this dependency analysis in my release-gate working papers, but it needs to be addressed before we can proceed.

The public package must exclude the training corpus entirely, although the source code and model weights may be released after that exclusion. I retained the record-level review in the privacy workpapers pending this approval meeting.

commitments.detail: Release the toolkit under AGPL-3.0-only and provide corresponding source for the linked toolkit code as required by the AGPL-3.0 core library dependency.
Exclude the training corpus entirely from the public package due to 37 customer support records containing personal data.
Exclude the benchmark package entirely from the public release due to customer-specific results whose disclosure is contractually prohibited.
Limit downloads of model weights to users in the United States and Canada only, and display an export-control notice on the repository reflecting this restriction.
